6: And the Philistines stopped up all the wells which his father’s servants had dug, etc. Isaac dug anew the wells (Genesis 26:15-18: For it is found (Berakhot 16b:13), "We only call three [people], 'fathers'" – meaning, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob." And this is difficult either way. If so, [either we could call all of the ancestors, "fathers" or] we could follow the first and only call Abraham, "father." And the explanation of the matter is that every righteous person has [some of his accomplishments] in the merit of his ancestors, but each one of the three "fathers" stood on their own [merit], as it is found in the midrash on the verse, I will remember My covenant with Jacob, etc. (Leviticus 26:42), each one stood on his own. Corresponding to this, the verse here says that all of the enlightenment that his father attained was stopped up afterward. So Isaac was forced to dig and clarify the proper path on his own. And this is also [the meaning of] that which is written, And there was a famine in the land – aside from the previous famine, etc. (Genesis 26:1). As it is found in the midrash, there were ten famines in the land. The understanding [of this] is that there are ten traits, corresponding to the ten utterances [with which God created the world] that the righteous must preserve, as it is found in Avot (5:1), "in order to give reward to the righteous, etc." And our father Abraham, peace be upon him, rectified [tikken] the trait of kindness and love and rectified the famine that was in his days. Afterward, there was another famine, etc. And so too with Jacob, etc. And the truth is that after each rectification, a new concealment came into being. And this is also [the meaning] of that which is written, one nation will contend with the other (Genesis 25:23). The explanation is like that which our sages, may their memory be blessed, said, "Whoever is greater than his fellow, accordingly is his [evil] impulse greater." And likewise, in whatever a person rectifies himself the most, the power of the impulse and the Other Side against him will be increased. And in this way, he increases the power of the [spiritual adversary] against him, and ascends higher. And this is what is customary, one level after another. And so, had the path of Abraham not been hidden, they would not have searched for a new path afterward. Hence, And there was a famine, etc., so Isaac needed to find the path of fear and restraint [gevurah] for himself. [Yet it is written, Do not descend to Egypt (Genesis 26:2), since the act of the father counts for the children, such that they do not need to actually do everything. The explanation is that Abraham went down to Egypt, and the holy Zohar explains that he needed to bring himself in to rectify all of the dangerous places, in order to nullify the famine from the Other Side, see there. And Issac was prepared for this, but it was said to him, Do not descend, etc., for the preparation for this was enough. And this is (the meaning of) that which is written, "Choose their paths, etc." (Bereishit Rabbah 76:4). That since he was prepared (to do) the act of his fathers, it did not have to actually be seen by him; rather (only) our father Abraham, peace be upon him – who was the first rectifier – needed to be tested by the ten tests in actuality. And this is (the meaning of) that which is written, In consequence that Avraham hearkened to my voice, etc. (Genesis 26:5). Hence, there was no further need to actually descend to Egypt. So does it appear to me.] And so, too, is there a need to rectify all ten levels mentioned above in every individual. But certainly our father Abraham, peace be upon him, truly feared God, as it is written, now I know that you fear God (Genesis 22:12). And [regarding] that which his trait was kindness and love, it is that he came to fear via love; and Isaac came to love via fear. Yet all of the traits are included in one another. And that is [the meaning of] that which is written, Isaac the son of Abraham, etc. (Genesis 25:19). And so too did Ramban, may his memory be blessed, write – that in matters of this world, love and fear contradict each other. For once one loves [someone], fear is not possible. But in the service of the Omnipresent, love and fear unite, etc. For true love is what brings one to fear, and likewise true fear is what brings one to love. So does it appear to me.
